context: Tatsuya-country teaches Sho-young how to read a clock face.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: Sho — can you read the clock?
lines.style: Slow, warm Tohoku drawl. Patient teaching voice—the kind that gives a child space to think. Gentle opening on the question.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: The hand is small. It's moving.
lines.style: Soft, genuinely observant. Not performing understanding, but noticing something real. Quiet wonder. Eyes on the clock.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 徐々に、覚えるんや、なんとなく感じて。
lines.en: You'll pick it up gradually. Just feel your way into it.
lines.style: Unhurried Tohoku cadence. Each phrase settling before the next. Tender reassurance—no rush, no pressure. A whisper of a smile.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 同じくらいの位置、何度も見る!
lines.en: The same place — I see it over and over!
lines.style: Bright, genuine excitement. The slight breathlessness of a child making a real discovery. Not performed—this actually matters to him.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: Oh—you've made real progress, haven't you.
lines.style: Warm recognition. Light surprise in the opening. Genuine praise, not excessive. The tone a grandfather uses when he's quietly proud of something he's watched happen.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、教えてくれて、嬉しい!
lines.en: Grandpa, thank you for teaching me. I'm so happy!
lines.style: Bright, open-hearted gratitude. The kind of unguarded joy only a child can offer. Warm and whole—no hesitation in the affection.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: やってきた成果や、頑張ったな。
lines.en: That's the fruit of what you've done. You really tried.
lines.style: Soft Tohoku warmth. Each word carries quiet weight. Tender pride—acknowledging his effort, not just the result. A moment held between them.
